source_snapshot.procedure: Generic setup says clear logs; display/check OEM demand logs; use `Save Logs`; then use `Clear All Logs`.
source_snapshot.criteria: All information/messages match status; OEM logs export and clear successfully.
source_snapshot.deepseek: YES assumes `/Managers/bmc/LogServices/OemLog/Entries`, disables TLS validation and returns only a read response while omitting WebUI/export/clear; it cannot establish proprietary semantics, pagination or no-risk.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION requires vendor schema/resource validation, complete retained export, clear authorization and recovery.

old_problem: The source deletes the representative OEM records before viewing/exporting them, supplies no stimulus to recreate them, then requests another clear. The assumed resource name does not define proprietary fields or severity, and service identity, decoder, complete export/raw payload and clear scope were unresolved.
disposition_reason: The review-layer flow can be fully defined without guessing an OEM command: discover the supported service, use a firmware-matched vendor schema/decoder to bind raw OEM records to WebUI rendering, validate a complete raw-capable Save Logs artifact, retain it externally, then perform one vendor-defined clear only after retention/FAE authorization. Exact proprietary identifiers are Project/vendor execution inputs.
decision_basis: XLSX row 863, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, selection manifest and historical record were directly reviewed.
OEM path labels and rendered strings are not authoritative field semantics; stable identity plus raw payload and the firmware-matched vendor decoder are required.
Viewer, Save Logs support artifact and Clear All Logs are separate functional checkpoints; a generic GET cannot substitute for any other checkpoint.
ED-03 permits a standard BMC draft but forbids guessed OEM parameters; ED-17 requires backup first; ED-20 preserves coverage; ED-38 requires one approved destructive action and no retry.

test_case.test_name: Verify vendor-decoded OEM Logs, complete support-grade Save Logs export, and one approved scoped clear
test_case.purpose: Verify the BMC OEM Logs page correctly represents a bounded, representative vendor-defined record set and statuses from stable raw OEM identities; verify `Save Logs` exports the complete intended service including support-required raw fields; then, after external evidence retention and fresh vendor/owner approval, clear exactly the authorized OEM service once and verify its documented isolated post-state.
required_package: Exact BMC/certificate, firmware/WebUI build, account role and discovered OEM LogService/resource identifiers
Firmware-matched vendor schema/decoder for stable ID, raw/OEM payload, component/source, message, status/severity, timestamp/timezone, sequence and WebUI rendering
Representative retained OEM-event dataset plus pagination, rollover, duplication, ordering and concurrent-record boundary rules
Save Logs filename/MIME/container, encoding/schema, inclusion of raw OEM fields, full-scope behavior, parser, checksum, redaction and support/custody acceptance
Vendor/support retention policy, clearable versus protected classes, exact clear control and expected empty/marker/sequence-reset semantics with excluded services
Dedicated lab target, protected credentials/trusted TLS, maintenance window, explicit FAE/owner clear authority, alternate OOB access and incident escalation
test_case.test_command: Do not pre-clear. Discover the supported OEM LogService from the target build; capture all pages, metadata, stable record IDs and raw OEM payload through trusted protected access. Bound concurrent writes and decode only with the matching vendor schema; compare component/message/status/severity/time presentation with the WebUI, preserving unknown fields as unresolved evidence. Invoke `Save Logs` once; quarantine, parse and checksum the artifact, reconcile all bounded IDs/raw fields/time coverage and confirm the artifact is usable by vendor support before external approved custody. Present the exact service, clearable records, retained artifact, excluded services and vendor-defined post-state and obtain fresh approval. Invoke the supported OEM clear once, then verify old-record disposition or marker/sequence behavior and that other log services remain unchanged. Never assume `/Managers/bmc/LogServices/OemLog`, use `curl -k`, expose passwords, infer unknown OEM meanings or retry clear.
test_case.expected_result: All representative OEM records are completely enumerated and their vendor-decoded WebUI fields match the authoritative raw payload and matrix. The Save Logs artifact is readable, complete, retains support-required raw data and is accepted into controlled custody. After fresh authorization, one clear affects exactly the OEM service/classes approved and reaches the documented marker/count/sequence post-state while unrelated logs and the retained artifact remain intact. No blanket pre-clear, guessed OEM semantics or repeated destructive action occurs.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires discovered service/build identity, authoritative schema/decoder, complete bounded raw-to-WebUI reconciliation, verified support-grade export, retention evidence, immediate exact-scope approval, one clear and isolated documented post-state with engineer/FAE verdict. HTTP success, one JSON page, UI text or file existence alone cannot pass. Unknown required fields, incomplete/raw-stripped export, wrong/multiple clear, cross-service deletion or unexplained record mismatch is FAIL. Missing vendor schema, representative data, export/retention contract or clear authority is NOT READY, not Pending or PASS.
safety_gate: Never execute the generic pre-test clear; it removes the representative OEM dataset and no safe source stimulus recreates it.
Do not infer proprietary meanings or severity from a URI or displayed string; retain raw payload and use the firmware-matched vendor decoder.
Do not assume ManagerId, LogServiceId, one-page completeness or HTTP 200. Discover the service and reconcile all pages by stable identity.
Use trusted TLS and protected credentials; OEM records may contain support-sensitive implementation details, so preserve controlled originals and policy-approved redactions.
A verified export preserves evidence but does not restore deleted live controller state. Clear only the approved disposable lab service after vendor/retention authorization.
Invoke clear exactly once and never retry automatically; stop on partial export, ambiguous scope, unsupported raw data, rollover, multi-service deletion, unknown response or access loss.
expected_evidence: Target BMC/certificate, firmware/WebUI build, role and discovered OEM service/schema/decoder identities
Complete bounded pre-clear record set with stable IDs, raw/OEM payload, decoded component/message/status/severity/time and pagination/sequence metadata
Redacted WebUI evidence and field-level reconciliation, explicitly preserving undecoded and presentation-only fields
Save Logs trusted origin, filename/MIME/size, checksum, parser result, stable-ID/raw-field completeness, custody and support-usability acceptance
Written vendor/retention authority, fresh exact-action approval, one clear request/response, expected marker/sequence behavior and unrelated-service proof
Protected audit, no-pre-clear/no-retry proof, limitations/recovery notes and engineer/FAE verdict
test_case.recovery: The controlled complete OEM export preserves support evidence but may not restore live BMC state. On wrong scope, unexpected deletion, unknown response or lost access, stop immediately, preserve action/audit evidence and invoke only the approved vendor/OOB incident path. Escalate protected or required record loss and never manufacture replacement OEM entries.

source_conflict.reason: ED-17 resolves the contradictory setup by retaining but prohibiting generic pre-clear. A representative existing dataset is viewed and exported first; the original final clear remains a separately authorized lab-only checkpoint.

blocked.reason: Viewer, export and clear functions are identifiable. Proprietary service/schema/decoder, representative data and retention/clear semantics are normal vendor/Project execution inputs, not a missing review decision.
